question: The most specific ultrasound sign of tubal ectopic pregnancy is a tubal ring (echogenic ring with a hypoechoic centre) seen in the adnexa separate from the ovary, with absent intrauterine gestational sac.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The tubal ring separate from the ovary is the most specific adnexal finding on TVS. A corpus luteum cyst can look similar but is within or immediately adjacent to the ovary.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A tubal ring separate from the ovary — a hyperechoic rim with a central hypoechoic area — is the most specific TVS sign of tubal ectopic pregnancy. Free fluid in the pouch of Douglas increases suspicion further.
